hints: Focus on how Period 3 oxides change across the period, from giant ionic to giant covalent to simple molecular.
Notice that Mg forms an ionic chloride while Al, Si and P all form covalent chlorides, so one option can be ruled out straight away.
Remember that only basic and amphoteric oxides react with acids, while acidic oxides like silicon dioxide do not, so check which remaining oxide neutralises HCl.
walkthrough:
**Use the oxide structure to narrow the list**

Think of Period 3 oxides from left to right. $\text{MgO}$ is giant ionic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is giant ionic with covalent character, $\text{SiO}_2$ is giant covalent, but oxides of P are simple molecular.

So a giant oxide structure points to Mg, Al or Si, not P.

**Use bonding with chlorine to remove another**

Now look at the chlorides. Mg is very electropositive so $\text{MgCl}_2$ is ionic. Al, Si and P are more electronegative so $\text{AlCl}_3$, $\text{SiCl}_4$ and $\text{PCl}_3$ are covalent.

Since X forms covalent bonds with chlorine, Mg is ruled out.

**Use acid-base behaviour to finish**

Oxides become more acidic across Period 3. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric so it reacts with acids and bases, while $\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic so it does not react with acids.

Reaction with acid:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 6\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Only aluminium fits all three clues, so X is Al.

options.A: Mg is incorrect. Although $\text{MgO}$ is giant and basic so it neutralises HCl, $\text{MgCl}_2$ is ionic, not covalent, because of the large electronegativity difference between Mg and Cl.
options.B: Al is correct. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ has a giant structure, $\text{AlCl}_3$ is covalent, and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric so it neutralises $\text{HCl(aq)}$ to form $\text{AlCl}_3$ and water. It is the only element that fits all three statements.
options.C: Si is incorrect. Although $\text{SiO}_2$ is giant and $\text{SiCl}_4$ is covalent, $\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic. It reacts with bases like NaOH but will not neutralise an acid like HCl.
options.D: P is incorrect. Although its chlorides are covalent, its oxides such as $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ have simple molecular structures, not giant structures, and they are acidic so they do not neutralise HCl.
